 (MR. ROHIT BANDAL - ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENTS  NO. 1 TO 4 / CLAIMANTS, MR. ARUN SHARMA - ADVOCATE  FOR RESPONDENTS NO. 5 AND 6 AND MR. ARVIND  KUMAR AGRAWAL - ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO. 7 /

This appeal coming on for hearing this day, the court p  following:
 JUDGMENT

Present miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the owner and driver of the offending truck bearing registration No. MP06-J-9048 against the award dated 25.3.2004 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Lahar, District Bhind in Claim Case No. 66/2001.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Lahar, District Bhind
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Appellants No. 1 and 2 are the owner and driver of the offending tractor No. MP06-J-9048 respectively, respondents No. 1 to 4 are the claimants, respondents No. 5 and 6 are the owner and driver of offending tractor No. MP30-M-1525 respectively and respondent No. 7 is the insurance company of tractor No. MP06-J-9048.

Cross-objections have also been filed by respondents No. 1 to 4 / claimants for enhancement of compensation amount and by respondent No. 7 - insurance company for dismissal or modification of the award.

The facts in brief to decide this appeal are that respondents No. 1 to 4 / claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for grant of compensation to the tune of Rs.6,50,000/- on account of death of deceased Rajkumar in a motor accident occurred on 12.9.2000 involving tractors bearing registration No. MP30-M-1525 and MP06-J- 9048.
Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the finding of learned claims tribunal in respect to apportionment of claim in respect to the appellants is against the settled principle of law.
In support of his submission, he has relied upon the case law of Sushila Bhadoriya and Ors. vs. M.P. State Road Transport Corporation and Anr.; (2005) 1 JLJ

entities.text: Sushila Bhadoriya and Ors. vs. M.P. State Road Transport Corporation and Anr.; (2005) 1 JLJ
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants argued that the findings of learned claims tribunal for apportionment of claim amount is well reasoned and as per the settled principle of law, therefore, present appeal be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
Sitaram & Anr. vs Mahila Sharda & Ors.

2 The perusal of record reveals that the claimants have examined AW- 1Sharda, AW-2 Dr S.K. Singh Niranjan, AW-3 Kalle @ Brij Kishor as well as produced relevant documents of charge-sheet pertaining to the criminal case related to this accident to prove its case.
The appellant no.-2 Bhagwati Prasad examined himself as DW-1 and stated that the deceased was not travelling in his tractor nor there was any accident by his tractor.
The perusal of evidence adduced by the parties reveals that nothing emerged in the cross-examination of claimants' witnesses to doubt the veracity of their statements.
There statements are also supported by the documents which are part of charge-sheet related to this accident.
Therefore, the defence of appellants is not found to be proved.

In view of the above, the learned trial court has rightly relied upon the evidence of claimants' witnesses and held that the accident occurred on account of contributory negligence of the drivers of both the offending tractors bearing registration No. M06-J-9048 and MP30-M-1525.

So far as apportionment of claim is concerned, in the case of Sushila Bhadoria (supra), at para 26, it is held that:
"There cannot be apportionment of claim of each tort-feasors in the absence of proper and cogent evidence on record and it is not necessary to apportion the claim."
and at para 27, it is held that "(i) Owner, driver and insurer of one of the vehicles can be sued and it is not necessary to sue owner, driver and insurer of both the vehicles.
Claimant may implead the owner, driver and insurer of both the vehicles or anyone of them, and (ii) There cannot be apportionment of the liability of joint tort-feasors.
In case both the joint tort-feasors are impleaded as party and if there is sufficient material on record, then the question of apportionment can be considered by the Claims Tribunal.
However, on general principle of law, there is no necessity to apportion the inter se liability of joint tort-feasors."
In the present case, from perusal of record, it is found that there is sufficient and cogent evidence on record to prove the contributory negligence of the drivers of both the offending tractors.

Since both the joint tort-feasors are impleaded as party and there is sufficient material on record against them,
therefore, learned claims tribunal rightly considered the question of apportionment.
It is pertinent to mention here that as per the above case law, choice for apportionment is not on the owners and drivers of the offending vehicles but it is available only to the claimants.
In view of the above, the appeal filed by the appellants has no substance and is hereby dismissed.

So far as cross-objection filed by respondent No. 7 - Insurance Company of Tractor No.
MP30-M-1525 is concerned, as discussed above, the contributory negligence of the driver of MP30-M-1525 is found to be proved which was insured with the company at relevant time,
therefore, the argument of learned counsel for the insurance company that learned claims tribunal has wrongly fastened the liability upon respondent No.7 - insurance company is not acceptable.
The learned counsel for the company argued that the driver of the MP30-M-1525 was driving the the Sitaram & Anr. vs Mahila Sharda & Ors.

3 said Tractor in breach of policy condition, therefore, company is not liable for compensation.
It is well settled that when the insurance company takes any defence, the same has to be proved by it by adducing cogent evidence.
However, in the present case, the company has not adduced any evidence to prove its defence.
In view of the above fact also, the arguments of learned counsel for the insurance company cannot be accepted.
Consequently, cross-objection filed by respondent No. 7 is hereby dismissed.

So far as cross-objection filed by respondents No. 1 to 4 / claimants for enhancement of compensation amount is concerned, learned counsel for the claimants argued that learned claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.1800/- per month.
He has further argued that the deceased was a Timber merchant and was earning Rs.4000/- per month.

However, the above arguments is not acceptable because to prove the aforesaid fact, no documentary evidence has been filed by the claimants, therefore, learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.1800/- per month.
However, as per the case law of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others; [2017 ACJ 2700], total compensation amount comes to Rs.3,91,600/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others; [2017 ACJ 2700]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the above, total amount of compensation comes to Rs.3,91,600/- (Three Lakh Ninety One Thousand Six Hundred only) and enhanced amount of compensation comes to Rs.1,33,800/-
(Rupees One Lakh Thirty Three Thousand Eight Hundred only).
The compensation amount be paid to the claimants within a period of 12 months from today failing which the enhanced amount of award shall carry penal interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by learned claims tribunal shall remain intact.
The court-fee be paid by respondents No. 1 to 4 / claimants as per rules prevailing at the time of filing of this miscellaneous appeal.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
